agreements: W33 closed at 4,376.16. After W32's sharp advance W33 turned to high-level consolidation, and the bullish structure is not confirmed broken.
DXY at 99.636 and a daily RSI of 38.39 lean supportive for gold, but the rate and volatility evidence is incomplete.
No chasing near 4,376. S1 V3.9 waits for a 30-minute close above roughly 4,397.78 and a fresh signal.
Every entry, stop and target must be reconfirmed on a live chart after the open.
The FOMC Minutes are the week's main event risk. Risk per trade is capped at 0.75%.
disagreements: The two reports ranked the primary scenario differently — one favoured range, the other bullish. Weighting them equally gives bullish 38%, range 38%, bearish 24%, which says direction is undecided.
They set different bearish trigger levels. 4,356.88 is taken as the early warning and a 4-hour close below 4,311.01 as confirmation, so an early warning is not mistaken for a completed reversal.
They named different S2 watch zones. Both 4,356.88–4,363.72 and 4,311.01–4,325.38 are listed as watch-only; without a fresh V3.2 reversal signal there is no entry.
Their secondary event lists differed. Both keep the FOMC Minutes as the main risk; other events need their official times rechecked before trading.
